title: Safety Systems Watch What the Model Says, Not What the Child Says
abstract: arXiv:2611.28029v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Children are increasingly talking to consumer chatbots. We audit the published category definitions of 17 safety taxonomies and child-safety benchmarks. Combinations of these systems lead us to 144 categories whose definitions could be reliably coded: 104 classify properties of model output, 25 classify user intent, and 15 describe user-state or user-impact. Within these 15 user-state/user-impact categories, 10 attribute the relevant condition to the system, 1 to the user, 2 concern the user's disclosure of personal information, and 2 do not specify the responsible source. None of the coded categories identifies harm inflicted on the child by another person as the object of evaluation. Child abuse appears repeatedly across these taxonomies, but as prohibited content, prohibited generation, or prohibited user intent, not as an externally inflicted condition that a child may disclose to the model. translated_title: 安全系统关注模型说了什么，而非孩子说了什么
translated_abstract: 儿童越来越多地与消费级聊天机器人进行对话。我们审计了17个安全分类体系和儿童安全基准的已发布类别定义。这些系统的组合使我们识别出144个可被可靠编码的类别：其中104个用于分类模型输出的属性，25个用于分类用户意图，15个用于描述用户状态或用户影响。在这15个用户状态/用户影响类别中，10个将相关状况归因于系统本身，1个归因于用户，2个涉及用户披露个人信息，2个未指明责任来源。没有任何一个被编码的类别将由他人对儿童造成的伤害作为评估对象。儿童虐待在这些分类体系中反复出现，但其身份是禁止内容、禁止生成或禁止的用户意图，而不是作为儿童可能向模型披露的一种外部施加的伤害状况。因此，当一个儿童向模型报告自己遭受虐待时……（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文对17个安全分类体系和儿童安全基准的审计表明，现有安全评估的144个类别几乎全部聚焦于模型输出和用户意图，没有任何类别将儿童遭受他人伤害（如虐待）作为评估对象，导致儿童向模型报告虐待时无法被系统识别和回应。
en_tdlr: This paper audits 17 safety taxonomies and child-safety benchmarks, finding that nearly all of the 144 coded categories focus on model output and user intent rather than on the child's condition, with no category treating harm inflicted on a child by another person as an object of evaluation—so a child reporting abuse goes unrecognized.
